story_pergunta: At your company, who approves what the AI is allowed to do?

slides.eyebrow: AI ON THE RISE · CHATGPT WALLET
slides.headline: AI agents can now pay. Is yours ready to be trusted with a card?
slides.sub: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet. Approval limits come first.

slides.headline: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet for agent purchases
slides.body: Agents can now complete purchases for the user. Each purchase needs a security check like Face ID, which creates a record. Agents pay with a token, not the real card. Limited rollout to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers.

slides.label: people use ChatGPT each week, per OpenAI
slides.sub: Many use it to research products, compare options and decide what to buy.

slides.headline: What I see in companies: the agent is the easy part
items: Nobody defines what the agent may do alone and what needs a human approval
Actions happen with no trail, so no one can explain a wrong order later
The agent goes live and nobody measures how many chats become real orders

slides.headline: A building materials store in southern Brazil, from question to order
items: 13,312 products in the ERP, 136 ways of writing the unit, 245 slang synonyms mapped
Search answers in milliseconds and hands 8 results to the model, which never sees the catalog
Rules: no made-up specs, never reveals stock, no discounts. 65 of 65 real questions found the product

slides.headline: Measure instead of assuming.
slides.body: An agent that can pay is only useful with approval limits, a trail of every action and a measured conversion rate. Build those before you hand it a card. OpenAI itself says spending limits are still a future step.

slides.eyebrow: WANT TO SEE HOW I DID IT?
slides.headline: Comment SDR.
slides.body: I'll send you the step-by-step of this case by DM. I take AI off the drawing board and put it into production, with measured results.

caption:
OpenAI announced ChatGPT Wallet. AI agents can now complete purchases for the user, with a security check like Face ID on every purchase and a record of each approval. It starts as a limited rollout to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers. OpenAI also says spending limits and categories are planned for later.

What I see in companies is that the agent itself is the easy part. The hard part is deciding what it may do alone, keeping a trail of every action, and measuring how many conversations turn into real orders.

I already built the step right before payment. For a building materials store in southern Brazil, I built an AI sales rep on WhatsApp. The ERP has 13,312 products and 136 different ways of writing the unit of measure. I mapped 245 counter-slang synonyms. The AI never sees the catalog: a simple search answers in milliseconds and hands 8 results to the model. The flow has 9 nodes, and the rules are clear: no made-up specs, never reveals stock, never gives discounts. 65 out of 65 real customer questions found the right product.

My view: build limits, trail and measurement before you give an agent a card.

Comment SDR and I'll DM you how I did it.

Sources: openai.com, techcrunch.com
